title: A / an, the and zero article 1

sections.title: The vs Zero Article vs A / an
sections.content:
We usually use the when we talk about things which are unique; that is, there is only one of them (or one set of them):
• the world, the sky, the atmosphere, the sun, the ground, the climate, the horizon, the human race, the environment, the travel industry, the internet
We use the with general geographical areas (e.g., the beach, the town, the sea(side), the land, the country(side)) and with time (the past, the present, the future).
Note, however, that some nouns like this can be used with zero article (i.e. no article) to refer to a concept in general:
• Climate is one of the many factors involved in changing farming methods. (or The climate ...)
• These flowers grow best in sandy soil and sun. (= sunshine)
If we want to describe a particular instance of these we can use a / an. Compare:
• I could see the plane high up in the sky. and When I woke up there was a bright blue sky.
• What are your plans for the future? and She dreamt of a future where she could spend more time painting.

sections.title: Generalisations about classes of things
sections.content:
We can use the when we make generalisations about classes of things using singular countable nouns. Compare the use of the and a / an in these sentences:
• The computer has revolutionised publishing. (this refers to computers in general) but not A computer has revolutionised publishing. (not an individual computer)
• The computer is an important research tool. and A computer is an important research tool. (this statement is true of both the general class and the individual item)
As an alternative to the + singular countable noun we can use a plural countable noun to talk about a class of things:
• Computers are an important research tool.
Note that if the is used with plural and uncountable nouns we refer to a specific thing or group:
• The computers have arrived. Where shall I put them?
• The music was wonderful. I could have listened to the orchestra all night.
When we define something or say what is typical of a particular class of people or things, we generally use a / an rather than the:
• A corkscrew is a gadget for getting corks out of bottles.
• A garden is there to give you pleasure, not to be a constant worry.

sections.title: Countable vs uncountable meanings
sections.content:
Some nouns can be used uncountably when we talk about the whole substance or idea, but countably when we talk about particular instances of it. When these nouns are used countably we can use a / an (and plurals). Compare:
• I don't drink coffee. and Would you like a coffee? (= a cup of coffee)
• He shook with fear. and He has a fear of heights.
There are many other nouns like this, including conversation, iron, pleasure, shampoo, sound. Some of these nouns (e.g. iron, paper) have different meanings when they are used countably and uncountably.

exercises.question: I think the best Australian wine is as good as any in ___ .
exercises.hint: Use 'the' for things which are unique (only one of them).
exercises.explanation:
Answer: the world
Use 'the' for things which are unique (only one of them). The grammatical signals in this sentence — the key words, connectors, or context — require this specific form. Look for these signals to make the same choice independently.

exercises.sentence: The life is full of unexpected surprises.
exercises.correction: Life is full of unexpected surprises.
acceptable: Life is full of unexpected surprises.
exercises.hint: Abstract nouns used in a general sense take zero article: Life, love, death, happiness.
exercises.explanation:
Answer: Life is full of unexpected surprises
When referring to abstract concepts in a general, philosophical sense (life, love, death, beauty, happiness, truth), use NO article. 'The life' would mean a specific life already identified. 'Life' without an article = life in general, the human experience.

exercises.question: As a child, Dariya would often daydream about travelling forward in time to ___ very different from the one she lived in.
exercises.hint: Use 'a' when describing a particular instance or type of future.
exercises.explanation:
Answer: a future
Use 'a' when describing a particular instance or type of future. The grammatical signals in this sentence — the key words, connectors, or context — require this specific form. Look for these signals to make the same choice independently.

exercises.sentence: I had the dinner at a very expensive restaurant last night.
exercises.correction: I had dinner at a very expensive restaurant last night.
acceptable: I had dinner at a very expensive restaurant last night.
exercises.hint: 'Have dinner/breakfast/lunch' — meals take zero article in fixed expressions.
exercises.explanation:
Answer: I had dinner at a very expensive restaurant
Meal names (breakfast, lunch, dinner, supper) normally take zero article in standard British and American English: 'have breakfast', 'eat lunch', 'cook dinner'. Use 'the' only when specifying a particular meal: 'The dinner we had last night was excellent'.

exercises.question: We get some strange requests in our shop. We had ___ in the other day who wanted to buy chocolate-covered ants.
exercises.hint: Use 'a' to refer to a particular but unspecified individual.
exercises.explanation:
Answer: a customer
Use 'a' to refer to a particular but unspecified individual. The grammatical signals in this sentence — the key words, connectors, or context — require this specific form. Look for these signals to make the same choice independently.

exercises.sentence: She plays piano beautifully — she's been learning since she was five.
exercises.correction: She plays the piano beautifully — she's been learning since she was five.
exercises.hint: Musical instruments use 'the' when referring to playing the instrument.
exercises.explanation:
Answer: She plays the piano beautifully
When referring to playing a musical instrument, use 'the': play the piano, play the violin, play the guitar. This is one of the few cases where 'the' is used with singular countable nouns in a general sense. Exception: in jazz contexts, musicians often omit 'the': 'She plays piano'.

exercises.question: The campaign against smoking in public places argues that its harmful effects are not confined to ___ .
exercises.hint: Both 'the smoker' (general class) and 'a smoker' (generalization true of an individual item) are possible.
exercises.explanation:
Answer: the smoker / a smoker
Both 'the smoker' (general class) and 'a smoker' (generalization true of an individual item) are possible. The grammatical signals in this sentence — the key words, connectors, or context — require this specific form. Look for these signals to make the same choice independently.

exercises.prompt: Add the correct articles to form a natural sentence:
exercises.hint: Unique nouns (the sun) and cardinal directions (the west) take 'the'
exercises.explanation:
Answer: The sun sets in the west
Use 'the' before unique objects (the sun, the moon, the earth, the sky) and before compass directions used as nouns (the north, the south, the east, the west). Note that when used as adjectives, no article is needed: 'western Europe', 'northern Scotland'.

exercises.question: Most red meat is relatively high in ___ .
exercises.hint: When talking about the whole substance, 'iron' is uncountable.
exercises.explanation:
Answer: iron
When talking about the whole substance, 'iron' is uncountable.
